verdicts.evidence: lines 835-859: every control is wired (submit check, file change, Clear, example, Back, download, Import, Show more, filters, Stop); result buttons get handlers at 738, 749-771. Each does what its label names.

lines 566-621, 628-662: counts and rows come from the user's list and api.validateImport; 684-691 progress from api.runImport. Example rows (818-832) load only on request and are labelled 'These are not real contacts' (841). Tally 0s are in a hidden section.
lines 582-616: review step shows good/bad counts, breakdown and the rows; 701-702 importing heading names how many contacts; 744-768 result restates imported, remaining and left-out counts.

Back keeps the textarea (854) and a failed check keeps it (557-561), but nothing is persisted: no sessionStorage/localStorage/URL state anywhere, and the textarea has autocomplete=off (221). A reload loses the pasted list, the review and any unfinished import queue.

lines 770 and 840 use window.confirm, whose default button (Enter) is OK. OK discards the contacts not yet imported (reset, 777-782) or overwrites the pasted list with example data. The default is the data-losing choice.
One page: paste, Check contacts (235), review, Import (257), outcome. The review step is required by the brief and guards the import; no extra screens or dialogs on the main path.

line 229 and 818-842: 'Fill in example data' button with 12 hardcoded sample contacts matches no task in the brief. Also CSV downloads of problem rows and remaining rows (259, 675-681, 767-768) were not asked for.

line 235 only Check contacts is primary on step 1 (file label is plain .btn); 257 Import primary on review, Back becomes primary only when Import is hidden (605-607); result has one primary (749 or 766).
Destructive controls are secondary: Clear is a small link (228), 'Start a new import' is a plain button placed last (769), neither is primary nor bound to Enter. Stop import is a plain button (297).

lines 534-541: controls are disabled only while the check runs, with the button reading 'Checking N rows...'. Stop is disabled only while stopping, with 'Stopping...' and a note beside it (727-729). Import is hidden, not disabled, when nothing is importable (605).
No title attributes, tooltips or hover cards anywhere in the markup or script.

Visible text (201-298, 448-519, 558, 741-772) is about contacts, rows and the CRM. No mention of frameworks, the request, mock data or unfinished features. The example-data note (841) describes user-loaded sample rows.

line 201: the lede carries the caveat 'Nothing is imported until you have reviewed the list and confirmed' at the top of every step, away from any decision (the same caveat sits by the Check button at 236). Line 262 adds a 'Tip:' callout.

Text narrates the interface: 217 'Paste from your spreadsheet export, or choose a file below'; 227 'or drag a file onto the box above'; 262 'Tip: download the problem rows...'; 591 'You can import the good rows now ... or go back and fix the list first'; 482 'Check the table below'.

'Nothing is imported' is said at 201, 236 and again at 589/591. 'Add your list' is both the step label (204) and the heading (213). The tip at 262 restates the download button, and 741 repeats it. 'will be left out' appears in the tally (585) and per-row tag (649).
Copy is factual throughout (201-298, 746-764): no greetings, slogans, superlatives, congratulations or exclamation marks. Success heading is 'N contacts imported' (746).

line 228 'Clear' names no object though a file chooser and a text box are both in view; line 258 'Back to edit the list' does not start with a verb. Others are specific ('Check contacts', 'Import the N good contacts', 'Stop import').

lines 502-521 translate REQUIRED, EMAIL_FORMAT, PHONE_FORMAT, DUPLICATE_IN_CRM into plain wording; table headers are Row, Name, Email, Phone, Company, Status (277-278). name/email/phone/company in the hint are the user's own column names. Raw error text is judged under COPY-011.

lines 531, 558-559 and 761: the error boxes add a 'Technical details' disclosure that prints the raw exception message ('ECONNRESET: socket hang up while trying to validate import', 'ETIMEDOUT: upstream timed out during batch 5'). The main sentence is fine but library messages are shown.

Messages at 448-497, 504-519, 558, 754-760, 793-813 state the problem ('We could not check your contacts because the CRM server did not respond', 'The import did not finish'). No 'invalid', 'failed', 'oops', exclamation marks or blame.

The table never renders empty: empty paste and header-only lists get messages with the next step (448, 497), filters are hidden when one group is empty (611, 616). Zero good rows: 590 says nothing can be imported and Back becomes the primary action (605-607).

Distinct text per cause: nothing pasted (448), column names but no contacts (497), every row has a problem (590), check could not reach the server with instruction to check again (558). Filters cannot yield an empty table (611).

lines 557-561: failed check shows a persistent message in the form, keeps the list, focuses Check contacts for retry. 716-721, 752-768: failed import states saved and remaining counts and offers 'Import the remaining N contacts' from the kept queue.

lines 547-548, 539: the Check button shows a spinner and 'Checking N rows...' at once. Import (8-15 s) shows 'X of N contacts imported', a progress bar and an estimate (293-295, 684-691) plus a working 'Stop import' (297, 723-731) using the AbortSignal.

While checking, the input step stays with a busy button; the review section with its 0 tallies stays hidden until buildReview runs after the response (563, 618). Import start shows 'Starting...' not a zero count (704).

td overflow-wrap (156, 193), table-wrap scrolls (149), rows paged 100 at a time with Show more (374, 657-661), numbers via toLocaleString (359). Missing values resolve to '' (492) and render as a blank cell or 'missing' (640-642); no undefined/NaN path.

line 861: the beforeunload prompt fires only while state.importing. Closing or navigating away with a pasted or hand-corrected list, on the review step, or with an unfinished import queue on the result step gives no prompt, and nothing is restored on return. Clear (838) also wipes the box unasked.

lines 216-219: the hint under the label states before any input that the first line must be the column names name, email, phone, company and that name and email are required; the placeholder (222) shows the shape.
The form has a single input (the CSV text, with the file chooser as another way to fill it); there is no mix of required and optional form fields.
line 835: validation runs only on submit (prepare, 544-545). The input listener at 836 only clears an existing error while typing; it never raises one.

line 232: the error box sits inside the form directly under the text box and file row, as bordered text, not a toast. Per-row problems are shown in the row itself with 'missing', a 'Will be left out' tag and sentences (636-652).
lines 545 and 557-561: on a client or server rejection the textarea value is never touched; only readOnly is toggled (536). The message even says 'your list is still here'.

line 545: on a rejected list the textarea gets aria-invalid=true and focus; it references the message via aria-describedby='csv-hint input-error' (221). On a server failure focus goes to Check contacts and the role=alert box announces it (232, 558-560).

The submit button is enabled on load (235) and disabled only during its own request (536). Submitting an empty box shows 'There is nothing to check yet. Paste your contacts into the box or choose a CSV file.' (448, 545).

lines 536, 835: the Check button is disabled with a busy label during the request and the submit handler ignores submits while disabled. startImport returns early if state.importing (693) and the review step is hidden once it starts.

Check switches to a spinner label synchronously (547-548); Import switches to the progress view (705); Stop becomes 'Stopping...' at once (727-729); filters flip aria-pressed and re-render (623-627); Clear and example fill change the box immediately (838-842).

Check ends in the review step or a stated failure (557-563). Import ends in a result view stating imported, remaining and left-out counts for done, stopped and failed cases (744-772). File load shows 'Loaded name (N lines)' and fills the box (807-809).
The only success message is the outcome view 'N contacts imported' (745-747), which reports a server-side result not otherwise visible. There are no toasts confirming visible changes.
No timers dismiss messages. The input error stays in place until the user edits the list or resubmits (543, 836); the import outcome and its action buttons stay until the user picks one (752-771).

line 838: Clear wipes the list at once with no undo (a programmatic value change also drops browser undo). Line 840: replacing the list with example data, which the page could simply restore, is guarded by a confirm dialog instead of running with undo.

line 770: discarding the unfinished import uses window.confirm 'N contacts have not been imported. Start a new import anyway?' with the browser's OK and Cancel; line 840 likewise for overwriting the list. Buttons do not name outcomes and OK, the losing choice, is the default.

Only two confirmations exist: overwriting a non-empty list with example data (840) and abandoning an import with contacts still not imported (770). Both are uncommon and guard loss; none guards save, cancel, close or the routine path.
No optimistic updates: the review is built only after validateImport resolves (563) and progress and results are driven by server callbacks (710-721).
The only modals are native window.confirm calls (770, 840), each a single yes/no decision opened by the user's own click. The multi-step flow itself is in-page sections, not a modal.
lines 770 and 840 use the browser's native confirm, which takes and traps focus, closes on Escape, has a visible Cancel and returns focus to the page on close.

Step 1 is heading, one line, then the list box and Check button (212-238). The review opens with the good/bad counts and the Import decision (246-260), then the problem rows table (272-283), filtered to problems first (616). Nothing decorative outranks the task.
lines 200-207: an h1, one muted sentence and a three-step indicator precede the working card. No hero, greeting banner or introductory panel.

lines 246-252, 582-598: the only summary numbers are contacts ready to import and rows with problems, with a breakdown by problem type. They inform the brief's decision whether to go ahead with the good rows.

lines 265-270, 611-616, 625: the active filter is a labelled pressed button directly above the table ('Problems (3)', 'Ready (9)'), each with its count, and 'All rows (N)' clears it in one action. 658 adds 'Showing X of Y rows' when paged.

All controls are native buttons, a textarea and a file input that stays focusable (117) with a focus ring on its label (118); the form submits from the button (835). Drag and drop (843-852) has the file chooser and paste as keyboard routes. No focus traps.

Row status has text tags 'Ready' / 'Will be left out' plus sentences (646-650); flagged empty cells say 'missing' (641); outcome icons are a tick and '!' with a heading (745, 753); selected filter is bold and aria-pressed (147); errors are text boxes.

line 209: a role=status live region exists on load and is filled via announce (403) for checking, review results, file loaded, import start, stopping and finish (548, 619, 706, 730, 751, 772, 810). The error box has role=alert from load (232); the bar is a progressbar with valuetext (294, 688-689).
The only disclosure is 'Technical details', built as a native details/summary element (531, 761). Filter toggles carry aria-pressed that updates with state (267-269, 625).

lines 177-195: under 640px the table becomes stacked label/value cards with data-label, action buttons go full width, the textarea uses 16px text, padding shrinks. Steps and filters wrap (66, 145); tally grid collapses (138). No fixed widths exceed 375px.
